label: Week of Nov 23–29, 2026
lede: One board met this week — Bunnell, on Monday night, Nov. 23 — and its wastewater vote and rezonings are still unreported, though the commission unanimously approved the interim manager's clean-up steps. The week’s biggest stories were money: the Sheriff’s Office returned $4 million in unspent funds to the county, and reporting put the county’s Amendment 3 budget cuts at about $60 million. Everything below is drawn from the same verified items on the map, grouped by topic.

items.headline: Amendment 3 fallout: FlaglerLive reports the county faces 'cataclysmic' cuts of about $60 million.
bullets: Amendment 3 fallout: FlaglerLive reports the county faces 'cataclysmic' cuts of about $60 million, layoffs, and potential new fees and taxes. The County Commission and Sheriff are exploring a special taxing district to pay for policing countywide. Flagler County voters backed Amendment 3 with 68%. (First reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 10, 2026)
County unemployment held steady at 5.2% in October (vs. 4.3% statewide, 4.1% nationally), though the workforce shrank by more than 200. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 23, 2026)

Week 1 at this building (Nov 16–17): the BOCC approved the 1-year, $350,000 Humane Society animal-control contract 5–0, and the County Commission unanimously selected Kim Carney as chair and Pam Richardson as vice chair — full record in the timeline below.
items.next: No County Commission meeting this week. Next regular meeting Mon Dec. 7, 2026, 9:00 a.m. — with a 9:30 a.m. public hearing on a resolution to use a uniform collection method for fire rescue assessments in unincorporated areas plus Beverly Beach, Bunnell, and Marineland, effective Oct. 1, 2027. (Source: public-hearing notice, noticeregistry.com.)

items.headline: The city closed on its $17M Town Center land deal — 23 parcels, about 259 acres.
bullets: The city closed in November on its $17 million purchase of 23 parcels — about 259 acres — in Town Center, settling its lawsuit with Palm Coast Holdings/Allete. Council approved the deal 4–1 on Aug. 19, 2026; an $11 million loan to pay for it was approved Oct. 20. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 9, 2026; purchase details also reported by David Stanley Realtor and Coastal Homes & Properties)
The Promenade at Town Center held its ribbon-cutting Mon Nov. 17 (4–6 p.m.); its 204 apartments are now leasing. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 18, 2026)

Week 1 at City Hall (Tue Nov 17): Tony Amaral Jr. (D2), Ray Stevens (D3) and Darlene Shelley (D4) were sworn in, Ty Miller was named Vice Mayor 4–1, the charter amendment results were certified, and two budget amendments passed unanimously — full record in the timeline below.

City Manager Mike McGlothlin's first-year evaluation — a combined 3.52 out of 5, 'meets expectations' — was not discussed in open session, and he received no raise. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 23, 2026)
Amendment 3 would cost Palm Coast $21.7 million by 2028 — 47% of its property tax revenue. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 4, 2026)
items.next: No City Council meeting this week. Next business meeting Tue Dec. 1, 2026, 6:00 p.m. — the tentative calendar lists second readings of the Cascades/Seminole Trace land-use map amendment and master planned development. No full Dec. 1 agenda published yet, so whether the asphalt plant (Planning Board recommended approval 6–1 on Nov. 18; Council needs a 4-of-5 supermajority) is on it is unconfirmed. (Source: Palm Coast Storylines, Oct. 6 agenda worksheet)

items.headline: School Board unanimously approves $3M — the YMCA clears its final hurdle.
bullets: Tue Nov 17: the Flagler County School Board unanimously approved a 35-year lease contributing $3 million toward building the new Volusia/Flagler YMCA in Town Center.
Per FlaglerLive, public dollars will fund 68% of the facility. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 18, 2026)

Deal terms per FlaglerLive: district swim teams get free access to an Olympic pool; the district can close the aging Belle Terre facility, saving at least $200,000 a year once construction finishes. Palm Coast signed a similar $3 million deal, enabling it to shut down the Frieda Zamba pool. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 18, 2026)
The Observer notes the board and YMCA agreed to two more amendments as part of the final approval. (Reported by Brent Woronoff, Palm Coast Observer, Nov. 18, 2026)
Context: planned ~$14M YMCA on city land — 35-year lease at $1/year, Olympic-size pool that school teams would use. City approved its $3.25M share Oct 20, contingent on the School Board's $3M share.

Sources: FlaglerLive email alert, Nov. 18, 2026, 2:49 p.m. ET — “Public Dollars Will Fund 68% of Palm Coast YMCA as Unanimous School Board Vote Commits $3 Million” (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 18, 2026); corroborated by The Observer email, Nov. 18, 2026 — “Palm Coast YMCA clears final hurdle as School Board approves lease agreement” (Reported by Brent Woronoff, Palm Coast Observer, Nov. 18, 2026; first reported by the Palm Coast Observer).
Quiet this week so far — no new meeting or news found for Nov. 23–29.
items.next: Approved Nov 17 at the Government Services Building — the final $3M hurdle is cleared. Next to watch: construction planning for the Town Center site.

items.headline: Nov. 23 agenda is out — the wastewater money vote leads a packed night. Outcome pending.
bullets: The Nov. 23 meeting happened at 7:00 p.m. FlaglerLive covered the meeting's clean-up presentation (see below), but the votes on Resolution 2026-16 (wastewater facility plan / State Revolving Fund) and the rest of the agenda remain unreported as of Wed Nov. 25 — no minutes posted. The meeting was livestreamed on the city's YouTube channel.

Interim City Manager David Brannon told the commission Monday evening that contracts had been signed without authority, an $835,000 budget error had been found, and other problems surfaced after former City Manager Alvin Jackson's departure. The commission unanimously approved Brannon's clean-up steps and named Commissioner Adkinson to a committee. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 24, 2026)

What was on the agenda: Resolution 2026-16 (wastewater facility plan / SRF); Ordinances 2026-20 and 2026-21 (rezoning about 14.92 acres to Commercial-Medium / B-1 Business District) and Ordinance 2026-22 (rezoning about 0.92 acres from Industrial to Single Family-Medium Density), all second reading; Resolution 2026-17 (FY2025-2026 budget amendment); the city's 2027 legislative priorities; amending the cold-weather shelter agreement with Flagler County; appointing a member to the Planning, Zoning and Appeals Board; and consent items (renewing the generator-maintenance agreement with Ring Power, sewer manhole inspection/rehabilitation, and a street-sweeping agreement). (Source: City of Bunnell Agendas & Minutes page)

Why Res. 2026-16 matters: approving the wastewater facility plan and sending it to the Florida Department of Environmental Protection is the step required to unlock the city's awarded State Revolving Fund (SRF) SA-HMW funding — the Supplemental Appropriation for Hurricanes Helene and Milton and the Hawaii Wildfires — for wastewater treatment plant improvements.

City news: storm debris collection began Mon Nov. 23 (separate piles for yard waste, construction debris, and appliances). A portion of E. Woodlawn St. between W. SR 100 and N. Anderson St. is closed until further notice — impassable from storm flooding/damage. City offices are closed Thu–Fri Nov. 26–27 for Thanksgiving; no trash service Thu Nov. 26. City Manager applications are open through Dec. 31, 2026. (Source: City of Bunnell news page, bunnellcity.us)

Recent context: Oct. 28, in a special hearing, the Commission denied the contested Project Butterfly 610-acre landfill west of Bunnell after 18 appeals. This building is the city's new Administration & Police complex — city offices and the Bunnell Police Department are based here too.
items.next: Next regular meeting Mon Dec. 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. The Nov. 23 votes on Res. 2026-16 and the rezoning ordinances are still unreported — watch the City of Bunnell Agendas & Minutes page for the minutes.

items.headline: Won the county contract — after the county went almost a month with none.
bullets: Mon Nov 16: won the county's 1-year, $350,000 animal-control contract, 5–0 (~$29,166/month).
Covers mandatory services only: dangerous-dog investigations, neglect investigations, rabies quarantines, sheltering animals of detained owners, and help in declared emergencies.
County may exit on 90 days' notice. No audit requirement was added — that was the meeting's main fight (see GSB pin).

items.headline: Sheriff's Office returned $4M to the county; ICE jail contract details released.
bullets: The Sheriff's Office returned $4 million in unspent funds to county government at the end of October, including $3.2 million in excess federal payments from housing undocumented migrants for ICE — the first public disclosure of the size of the Sheriff–ICE detention contracts. The money goes into a capital reserve for the Sheriff's Office. (First reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 23, 2026)

Amendment 3 fallout: Sheriff Rick Staly ordered staff to prepare drastic cuts — 'everything is on the table,' from the helicopter to body cams to service cuts. He expects the agency to lose about $15.5 million next fiscal year, has canceled its patrol car order, enacted a hiring freeze, and frozen every vacant position; he has proposed a dedicated property tax to offset the loss. (Reported by Pierre Tristam, FlaglerLive, Nov. 10, 2026; Frank Fernandez, Daytona Beach News-Journal, Nov. 10, 2026; Craig Patrick, FOX 13, Nov. 22, 2026)
items.next: Watch whether the Sheriff's proposed dedicated property tax — and the special taxing district for countywide policing being explored with the County Commission — moves to a formal agenda item.

items.headline: Palm Coast's brand-new fire station — opened Oct 8, replacing the city's original 1977 firehouse.
bullets: Budget amendment — Fire Impact Fee Fund: city summary ties it to +$230,000 for higher Fire Station 22 costs. Passed unanimously. (Meeting record frames it as a FY25→FY26 carry-forward — both framings noted; packet is the tiebreaker.)

It replaces Palm Coast's original fire station — built in 1977 by ITT and donated to the Palm Coast Service District, at 307 Palm Coast Pkwy NE. The original building is being preserved and repurposed.

bullets: On Oct 20, 2026 the Palm Coast City Council approved revised plans for Lakeview Estates, the 280-acre former Matanzas golf course property (Reported by Brenno Carillo, Daytona Beach News-Journal, Oct. 21, 2026).
The changes: 39 more single-family homes (250 total, down from 272), 250,000 sq ft of neighborhood commercial on Tract 9 fronting US-1, and an ~11-acre community park on Tract 8.
Tract 9 sits on the east side of US-1, about 3,300 feet north of Matanzas Woods Parkway (city agenda packet).
Buffers were raised and a soil test for arsenic is required.

items.headline: Dec 7 hearing: the County Commission considers using the tax bill to collect fire-rescue assessments — and the department passed its state EMS inspection in full.
bullets: Mon Dec 7, 2026, 9:30 a.m., Board Chambers, 1769 E Moody Blvd, Bldg 2, Bunnell: the County Commission considers a resolution to use a uniform collection method (the tax bill) for fire-rescue assessments in unincorporated Flagler County, Beverly Beach, Bunnell and Marineland. Assessments would begin Oct 1, 2027 and continue annually unless the county ends them. (Source: public-hearing notice, Nov 12, 2026)
Flagler County Fire Rescue runs 13 stations across 571 square miles, staffed around the clock by paramedics and EMTs. (Source: flaglercounty.gov — Fire Rescue)
It passed its 2026 Florida Department of Health EMS inspection on Oct 27, 2026, all areas in full compliance.
